clue.text: Torment for the King at Agincourt

definitions.meaning: to torment is to harass or plague someone
Henry V, victor at Agincourt in 1415, goes by a familiar nickname in Shakespeare's play

explanation.surface: Agincourt was agony for the French king's side.
explanation.walkthrough: Shakespeare's Henry V is called Harry by his soldiers; to harry is to torment.
explanation.definitionFit: To harass someone is to plague them; Henry V is known by the familiar name Hal or this one in Shakespeare.

clue.text: Become friendly: card players do

definitions.meaning: to become affectionate, clasping each other's fingers
card players keep their dealt cards in their grip

explanation.definitionFit: Lovers clasp fingers as a sign of affection, while at bridge each player keeps a dealt set of cards.

clue.text: Bird first mentioned in tale by, Defoe

indicators.note: first mentioned keeps only the opening part of the title, dropping the rest

parts.note: Defoe's best-known tale is Robinson Crusoe

explanation.surface: A bird is said to appear first in a Defoe story.
explanation.walkthrough: Robinson Crusoe is Defoe's novel; its opening five letters are the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A small red-breasted songbird familiar in British gardens.

clue.text: City is the first to toast a member of the royal house

definitions.text: a member of the royal house

parts.note: York is a cathedral city in northern England

indicators.note: the first to picks the opening letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A city drinks the first toast to a royal.
explanation.walkthrough: The House of York was one side in the Wars of the Roses.
explanation.definitionFit: A supporter or member of the House of York, the dynasty of Edward IV and Richard III.

clue.text: Said to avoid offering a reservation

indicators.note: said tells us the words are spoken, so we want something that sounds like them

parts.note: to avoid is to miss, and offering is giving

explanation.surface: A diner talks of skipping the offering plate rather than booking a table.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Said' signals that MISS GIVING, spoken, gives the answer, spelt with one S.
explanation.definitionFit: A doubt or qualm held about something is a misgiving, and a reservation is just such a doubt.

clue.text: Cope with husband

definitions.meaning: to cope with is to handle or get by
to husband is to use resources carefully

explanation.definitionFit: Coping with a situation is handling it, and husbanding resources is administering them prudently.

clue.text: Glass vessel

definitions.meaning: a tall glass for sherry or beer
a sailing ship with fore-and-aft rigging

explanation.definitionFit: It is both a large drinking glass for sherry or beer and a two-masted sailing ship.

clue.text: Piece of zinc is ordered for this cutter

indicators.note: Piece of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone orders a bit of zinc for a cutting tool.
explanation.definitionFit: A front tooth with a sharp edge used for biting, so a natural cutter.

clue.text: Sixth sense apparent in education

parts.note: tuition is teaching, education

explanation.surface: Extra perception is evident in someone's schooling.
explanation.definitionFit: Knowing without reasoning is the instinct popularly called a sixth sense.

clue.text: Letters on English Xmas fare

parts.note: gees are the letter G written out, plural

explanation.surface: Letters printed on an English Christmas menu.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' puts the letters above E.
explanation.definitionFit: Roast goose was the traditional Christmas dinner bird in England before turkey.

clue.text: Student represents any birth as a tortuous proceeding

parts.note: L is a learner, the student driver's plate

indicators.note: represents read as re-presents, the letters set out again in a new order

explanation.surface: A student describes giving birth as a long, painful business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'represents' signals an anagram: the letters of ANY BIRTH become ABYRINTH, after L.
explanation.definitionFit: A maze is a winding, confusing affair, so any tortuous process can be called one.

clue.text: Prune that is a sweet one

parts.note: to prune is to cut back
i.e. abbreviates id est, that is

explanation.surface: A dried plum is described as a sugary treat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prune' looks like the fruit but is the verb meaning cut.
explanation.definitionFit: An attractive, endearing person is a sweet one, a darling.

clue.text: Old county fellows charge after the chase

indicators.note: after puts the fellows and their charge behind the chase in the answer

parts.note: the chase is hunting with hounds
dons are university fellows
a hire charge is a fee, so hire means charge

explanation.surface: Gentlemen in an old shire pay a fee after the fox hunt.
explanation.walkthrough: HUNTINGDONSHIRE was an English county, merged into Cambridgeshire in 1974.
explanation.definitionFit: This former English shire no longer exists as a separate administrative area, hence old.

clue.text: Deft attempt, throwing away the King, to finesse

parts.note: nice in its old sense of precise, delicately skilful

indicators.note: throwing away says the king's letter is dropped from the attempt

parts.note: an attempt is a try
R is Rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A skilful try at bridge discards the king as a clever finesse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'throwing away' removes R (Rex) from TRY, leaving TY.
explanation.definitionFit: A subtle detail or delicate refinement is a fine point of skill, a matter of finesse.

clue.text: Slight noise made opening safe with money in it

indicators.note: in it puts the money inside the safe-opening

parts.note: a safecracker is cracking it open
L is the pound sign, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: A burglar makes a faint sound opening a safe full of cash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in it' puts L inside CRACKING, between C and I.
explanation.definitionFit: A series of small sharp snapping sounds, like a fire or a bad radio line.

clue.text: One egg or an omelette fit for Kings

indicators.note: eggs are broken and mixed for an omelette, so these letters are scrambled

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A cook offers an egg or an omelette worthy of royalty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'omelette' signals an anagram of I with EGG OR AN.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes the period of the four Hanoverian monarchs named George, so it suits those kings.

clue.text: When day is done tops up at the club

parts.note: after the day comes the night

indicators.note: up in a down clue says the word tops is read bottom to top

explanation.surface: After dark someone tops up their drink at the club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses TOPS to give SPOT.
explanation.definitionFit: A nightclub is a place of evening entertainment, such as a club.

clue.text: Meets unexpectedly in school on March 15

parts.note: coll. abbreviates college, a school
the Ides of March fall on the 15th

explanation.surface: Two people bump into each other at school on the Ides of March.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ides of March was the day Julius Caesar was assassinated.
explanation.definitionFit: Crashing into something is meeting it by accident and with force.

clue.text: Evidence of a sudden stroke?

parts.note: a sudden stroke sounds like a seizure, but here it is a quick click of the camera, whose result is a casual photograph

explanation.surface: A doctor seeks proof that a patient had a sudden stroke.
explanation.definitionFit: A quickly taken photograph records a moment caught in an instant, a shot made in a flash.

clue.text: This drink sounds a deliberate trap

indicators.note: sounds says the answer is said like the words given

parts.note: deliberate is slow, and a gin is a snare or trap

explanation.surface: A drink's name suggests a carefully laid snare.
explanation.walkthrough: SLOE GIN is a liqueur of gin steeped with sloes, wild plums.
explanation.definitionFit: A liqueur made by steeping blackthorn berries in spirit, a red cordial.

clue.text: Drink strong beer after food

indicators.note: after puts the beer behind the food in the answer

parts.note: an egg is food
nog is a strong ale once brewed in East Anglia

explanation.surface: Someone orders a strong ale once they have eaten.
explanation.definitionFit: A drink of beaten egg, milk and often spirits, a festive beverage.

clue.text: Uses examples freely in theories

indicators.note: freely says the letters move about without fixed order

parts.note: egs abbreviates examples, e.g. in plural

explanation.surface: A writer uses examples liberally to support theories.
explanation.walkthrough: 'freely' signals an anagram of USES with EGS.
explanation.definitionFit: Hypotheses are conjectures, tentative answers not yet proved.

clue.text: After first quarter, lender becomes a paper maker

indicators.note: after the first quarter means the first two of eight letters of the lender are gone

parts.note: a creditor is one who lends money

explanation.surface: A moneylender becomes a newspaper boss after three months.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After first quarter' drops the first quarter, CR, of CREDITOR.
explanation.definitionFit: The person who runs a newspaper shapes each issue, the one who makes the paper.

clue.text: Recognition of clever dicks getting into the act

indicators.note: getting into puts the clever dicks inside the act

parts.note: taken as written, the word act
clever dicks are know-alls, playfully knowledge men

explanation.surface: Smart alecs push their way into the show to get noticed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clever dicks' are know-alls, punningly KNOWLEDGE MEN; the surface 'act' looks like a stage turn.
explanation.definitionFit: Acknowledging something is admitting or crediting it, so the noun is a form of recognition.

clue.text: A Spanish comrade of note in the past

indicators.note: in puts the note inside the word for the past

parts.note: ago means gone by, in time past
mi is the third note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A Spanish friend was once known for his music.
explanation.walkthrough: The opening 'A' belongs to the definition, though the surface makes it sound like a stray article.
explanation.definitionFit: In Spanish a friend or pal, used in English for a buddy.

clue.text: Steer clear of notice in the twilight

indicators.note: in puts the notice inside the twilight word

parts.note: eve is evening, twilight
an ad is a notice, advertisement

explanation.surface: Someone avoids attention under cover of dusk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'twilight' is the eve, evening; the surface makes 'notice' a verb, but it is a noun, an advert.
explanation.definitionFit: To dodge or escape something is to keep away from it.

clue.text: Formation dangerous for aircraft

parts.note: not a flying formation of planes but frozen water forming on the wings

explanation.surface: Pilots fear flying in close formation.
explanation.definitionFit: Frost building up on wings adds weight and spoils lift, a known hazard in flight.

clue.text: Device for marking the occasion

parts.note: not a celebration but an office tool that prints the day on documents

explanation.surface: Someone wants something to commemorate a special event.
explanation.definitionFit: An office tool inks the day, month and year onto papers, recording when they arrived.

clue.text: Engineer has quarter in garrison mess

indicators.note: in puts the quarter inside the jumbled garrison
a mess is a muddle, so the letters of garrison are jumbled

parts.note: E, east, is one of the four compass quarters

explanation.surface: A military engineer is billeted in the garrison's mess hall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mess' signals an anagram of GARRISON, and 'in' sets E within it.
explanation.definitionFit: One who engineers an event arranges and contrives it, a planner or fixer.

clue.text: "_____s to the _____ farewell!" (Hamlet)

parts.note: Gertrude scattering flowers on Ophelia's grave in Hamlet; the same word fills both blanks

explanation.surface: A line from Hamlet with two words missing.
explanation.walkthrough: Gertrude's line at Ophelia's burial is 'Sweets to the sweet: farewell!'; the answer fills both gaps.
explanation.definitionFit: The quotation needs a word meaning lovely or dear, which in plural also means confections.
